title: Mean efficiency of recorded plant turnover was 22 percent against early warm-site references in 20 gradients
abstract: We tested whether a small total amount of species turnover explains a remaining gap to warm-site plant communities. We used matched plot histories in 40 TransPlant contrasts from 20 mountain gradients. An exact L1 bound separates the minimum residual required by a limited change budget from any residual beyond that minimum. Recorded endpoint turnover averaged 0.901 initial-gap units, while the final gap was 0.871. The minimum residual was 0.194 and the remainder was 0.676. Mean net gap reduction per unit of recorded turnover was 0.216, with 95% gradient bootstrap limits 0.105 to 0.310. Requiring presence in two censuses at each endpoint gave 0.211. A final destination reference raised efficiency to 0.436, so reference time matters. These are empirical accounting results, not causal shares of ecological processes. Small plot samples, missed taxa, post-treatment initial censuses and combined transplant effects limit inference. The method distinguishes a total change restriction from changes that fail to reduce a chosen gap. It does not identify the cause of weak thermal tracking or reject species-specific lags. Source records stay external; code, proof, aggregate evidence, source hashes and reproduction instructions are included.
